Application Materials.content:
When you apply you’ll need to submit a personal statement explaining why you want to take the course. You’ll need to include information about:
- your knowledge of the subject area
- why you want to study a postgraduate qualification in this course
- how you intend to use your qualification
References are not required for this programme. Please include the required paperwork showing your first degree and your IELTS English language test score (if you are a non-native English speaker) with your application. Without these, your application may be delayed.

Interview Requirements.content: If you don't have the exact entry requirements, but you have significant work experience in this sector we’ll assess your relevant professional experience, your subject knowledge and your aptitude for learning. Your application will be considered on individual merit and you may be asked to attend an interview.

Application Deadlines.content:
**Logistics and Supply Chain Analytics (MSc)** starts **September 2026**.
- **UK students:** The deadline to apply for this course is **Wednesday 2 September 2026, midday UK time**. Applications may close before the expected deadline if places are filled.
- **International students:** The deadline to apply for this course is **Wednesday 19 August 2026, midday UK time**. Applications may close before the expected deadline if places are filled.

Academic Requirements.content:
You’ll need a **2.1 degree** in a subject which includes quantitative study such as:
- finance
- sciences
- maths
- engineering
- computer science
- economics
- quantitative business or management
The University might consider other subjects if you can show evidence of quantitative study. It does not accept the following subjects:
- Language Studies – degrees that focus on learning a language or how to translate, such as 'Business English', 'Applied English', or 'Translation', are not acceptable. However, this restriction does not apply to ‘English’ and ‘English literature’ degrees of the kind taught in the UK.
- Art/Design/Vocational Studies – degrees that focus on learning a particular form of art, craft or vocation. These include degrees in art, graphic design, photography, television broadcasting, script writing, or performance/dance.
If you don't have the exact entry requirements, but you have significant work experience in this sector, the University will assess your relevant professional experience, your subject knowledge and your aptitude for learning. Your application will be considered on individual merit and you may be asked to attend an interview.
For applicants from China: Southampton accepts bachelor's degrees (学士学位) from China. For postgraduate taught degrees, applicants usually need the equivalent of a **2:1 or a 2:2 undergraduate degree** from a highly ranked Chinese university, with a minimum average grade of between **70% and 83%**, depending on the university where they studied; the course page gives the exact requirement. Since this course requires a **2:1**, the Chinese equivalent 2:1 grades are:
| Tier | GPA out of 4.0 | GPA out of 5.0 | Percentage (%) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tier A | **2.8** | **3.5** | **70%** |
| Tier B | **3.1** | **3.88** | **75%** |
| Tier C | **3.25** | **4.06** | **80%** |
| Tier D | **3.7** | **4.63** | **88%** |
If a Chinese institution isn't listed, use the grades for **tier D**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
If English is not your first language, you must show that you can use English to the level required. [Visit our English language pages](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/studentadmin/admissions/admissions-policies/language.page) to find out which qualifications are accepted and how you can meet the requirements.
If taking IELTS, minimum scores are:
| IELTS component | Minimum score |
| --- | --- |
| Overall | **6.5** |
| Reading | **6.0** |
| Writing | **6.0** |
| Speaking | **6.0** |
| Listening | **6.0** |
If you do not meet the English language requirements through a test or qualification, you may be able to meet them by completing one of the University’s [pre-sessional English programmes](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/study/pre-sessional) before starting the course.
When applying, non-native English speakers should include the required paperwork showing their IELTS English language test score; without this, the application may be delayed.

Program Overview.content:
**Logistics and Supply Chain Analytics (MSc)** is a **Master of Science** course at the University of Southampton, starting **September 2026**. It is a **full-time**, **1 year** course based at **Highfield** and awarded by the University of Southampton.
Gain the expertise to manage the movement of goods, people, data or money across a supply chain on this master’s degree course. You’ll develop advanced management and analytical skills, and have the chance to work on a real business project during a 3-month industry placement. You’ll be taught by academics from one of the country’s leading analytics research groups, and graduate with the skills and knowledge for a successful career in logistics.
On this MSc Logistics and Supply Chain Analytics degree, you'll learn advanced management skills and the ability to use data to make good business decisions. You'll gain a thorough grounding in:
- integrated and international logistics supply chain management
- software and programming skills
- quantitative, qualitative and technical skills
You'll graduate from the course knowing how to:
- formulate a hypothesis and use data to test it
- use analytical techniques to support decision making
- develop computer-based decision support systems to gain insight from data
The course is taught in association with the University's cross-disciplinary [Centre of Operational Research, Management Sciences and Information Systems](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/cormsis/about/index.page) (CORMSIS), one of the largest groups of its kind in the UK. This means you'll benefit from a wider choice of optional modules which you can use to pursue your own interests or career plans. You can choose to specialise in the following aspects of logistics and supply chain management:
- Operational Research
- Risk Management
- Finance
- Sustainability
This is full-time master’s course. Your studies will last a full 12 months. For the first 8 months (semesters 1 and 2) you'll focus on the taught part of your course. Each semester is made up of a combination of modules that everyone on the course takes, and modules that we’ll ask you to choose from a list of options. For the remainder of the course, you’ll work independently on your dissertation. You’ll have one-to-one meetings with your supervisor during this time to discuss your progress.
You’ll carry out a research project resulting in a 15,000-word dissertation, on a subject of your choice (to be agreed with your supervisor). The project is a chance for you to develop your research skills and show in-depth knowledge of your chosen subject. You might have the chance to complete your project as a 3-month summer placement with an external organisation. We place more than 50 students in external projects every year.
Your course leader is [Dr Fangsheng Ge](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/people/5zbxnh/doctor-fangsheng-ge), Lecturer in Management Science.
Accreditation: [**Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB)**](https://www.aacsb.edu/).
Graduates commonly work in a range of organisations or sectors including: Airlines, Department of Transport, Education, Government Organisations, National Air Traffic Services, NHS, Royal Mail, Private companies, Third sector organisations.
Careers directly related to this course include:
- Inventory and warehouse manager
- Logistics engineer
- Logistics planner
- Supply chain analyst
- Supply chain manager
- Supplier relationship manager
- Vehicle fleet manager
- Vehicle route planner
Example job titles of Southampton MSc Logistics and Supply Chain Analytics graduates include Researcher, Management trainee, Business analyst, Data analyst, IT consultant, Logistics manager, Supply chain coordinator, Supply manager, Purchasing manager, and Management consultant.
Job prospects for MSc Logistics and Supply Chain Analytics graduates: **£33k Average professional salary**, **81% In a skilled profession or further study**, **95% Graduate employment rate**. Source: Example graduate job titles and job prospect statistics taken from The Graduate Outcomes Survey, which gathers information about the activities and perspectives of graduates 15 months after finishing their course.

Curriculum.content:
Logistics and Supply Chain Analytics (MSc) is a **full-time** course based at **Highfield**. It starts in **September 2026** and lasts **1 year / a full 12 months**.
Course structure:
- For the first **8 months** (semesters 1 and 2), students focus on the taught part of the course.
- Each semester includes a combination of modules that everyone on the course takes, and optional modules chosen from a list.
- For the remainder of the course, students work independently on a dissertation, with one-to-one supervisor meetings.
- Students may have the chance to complete the project as a **3-month summer placement with an external organisation**.
For entry in academic year **2026 to 2027**, Year 1 modules students **must study** are:
- [**Computational Methods for Logistics**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6542)
- [**Foundation of Business Analytics and Management Science**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6513)
- [**Integrated Logistics**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6314)
- [**Principles of Supply Chain Management**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6538)
- [**Simulation**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6122)
- [**Strategic Purchasing and Supply Management**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6316)
Students **must also choose from** the following modules:
- [**Advanced Analytics**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6554)
- [**Behavioural Operations**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6555)
- [**Credit Risk & Data Analytics**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6556)
- [**Dissertation (Analytics)**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6545)
- [**Forecasting**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6011)
- [**Python for Business and Marketing**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6182)
- [**Risk Taking and Decision Making**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6134)
- [**Sustainable Operations and Supply Chains**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6571)
Dissertation: students carry out a research project resulting in a **15,000-word dissertation**, on a subject of their choice to be agreed with the supervisor.
Learning activities include lectures, classes and tutorials, coursework, individual and group projects, and independent learning. Assessment is through coursework, essays, group assignments, written exams and a dissertation.

Financial Aid.content:
Southampton Business School (MSc) Dean Scholarship (International): Scholarships of **£9,000** and **£5,000** are available to international students studying an eligible postgraduate master’s at the University of Southampton Business School, including [MSc Logistics and Supply Chain Analytics](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/logistics-supply-chain-analytics-masters-msc "MSc Logistics and Supply Chain Analytics (8535)"). If you have a 1st or an equivalent qualification in your undergraduate studies you will get **£9,000**. If you have a 2:1 or an equivalent qualification in your undergraduate studies you will get **£5,000**.
Eligibility: To get this scholarship you must be an international student required to pay the oversees fees; have a conditional or unconditional offer to study an eligible course; achieve a 1st or an equivalent qualification in your undergraduate studies to receive a **£9,000** award; or achieve a 2:1 or an equivalent qualification in your undergraduate studies to receive a **£5,000** award. Students coming from China must have studied at a [Tier A](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/international/entry-qualification-equivalencies/china/postgraduate-taught-tier-list "Chinese awarding institutions listed by tier") university. There are a further 100 awards of either **£9,000** or **£5,000**, depending on applicant eligibility, for applicants coming from a [Tier B](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/international/entry-qualification-equivalencies/china/postgraduate-taught-tier-list "Chinese awarding institutions listed by tier") Chinese university; these scholarships will be issued on a first past the post basis with an additional eligibility requirement that applicants in this category pay their tuition fee deposit by **15th January 2026**.
How to apply: You do not need to apply to this scholarship. If you meet the eligibility criteria, we will award you this scholarship and let you know by email.

Multiple Applications.content:
If you would like to apply for both taught and research programmes, please complete a separate form for each application. If you want to apply for two taught programmes within the same Academic School please list these in order of preference as Choice 1 and Choice 2. If you want to apply for a taught programme in another School or any research programme, please fill in a separate form.
On the application form, Choice 2 should only be used if it is in the same Academic School as Choice 1: “Please only input a programme in Choice 2 if it is in the same Academic School as Choice 1. If not, please fill in a second application form.” The form also asks: “Are you applying for other programmes at the University of Southampton? Yes / No. If yes, please give details.”

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
Applicants in possession of an unconditional offer of a place may request that it be deferred to the next intake. The University does not typically permit more than a single deferral. For postgraduate taught study, applicants can make a request via their online application portal and requests for deferral will typically be accepted where there are unforeseeable life events and circumstances outside of the applicants’ control.
Reasons typically accepted for deferral include:
- Bereavement due to the loss of a close family member - a parent, grandparent, guardian, sibling, son, daughter or a close personal friend.
- Serious illness and health problems.
- Victim of a natural disaster.
- Victim of conflict and political unrest that prohibits travel to the UK.
- Personal accident or injury of a significant nature.
- Child care responsibilities or caring responsibilities.
- Relevant work experience/placements/internships.
- Military service.
- Change of employment circumstances.
- Unforeseen ATAS delays.
- Unforeseen Visa delays.
Reasons not typically accepted for deferral include:
- Unsuccessful in securing funding (e.g. scholarship) except in cases of the Sanctuary Scholarship.
- To undertake employment or travel unrelated to the degree programme applied for.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
If you do not meet the English language requirements through a test or qualification, you may be able to meet them by completing one of our [pre-sessional English programmes](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/study/pre-sessional) **before you start your course**.
If you don’t meet direct entry requirements, you can apply to complete a Pre-Master's programme through Southampton’s partnership with OnCampus. You'll progress to your chosen course after successfully completing the programme. [Find out more about Pre-Master's programmes for international students.](https://www.oncampus.global/our-study-centres/oncampus-southampton/progression-degrees)
